definition: Erroneous means containing error; factually incorrect.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word erroneous. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know erroneous should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The museum quietly corrected an erroneous caption that had the explorer sailing for the wrong king.
An imprecise figure is loose but circles the truth; an erroneous one has left the truth entirely.
Preposterous goes past erroneous — wrong so loudly that no one needs a fact-checker to see it.

Incorrect is the plain, all-purpose stamp for whatever is not right — an answer, a guess, a date. Erroneous means the same falseness in formal dress, stamped on entries, figures, reports, and beliefs by auditors and editors. Anything can be incorrect; erroneous files the finding on paper.

Inaccurate measures distance from the true value — a reading, a map, a quote can be inaccurate by a hair or by a mile. Erroneous is not a matter of degree: an erroneous entry has parted company with the truth, and no rounding brings it back.
matching the facts exactly

Erroneous means containing error; factually incorrect.
For a week the airline blamed the fog.

Then a scheduler noticed the real culprit: one erroneous entry in the crew database had Captain Weiss down as having left the airline, so the system had been grounding her flights while she sat, fully certified, in the pilots' lounge.
One wrong field, four hundred stranded passengers, and not a cloud to blame.
Erroneous is the exact word for that database entry: containing error, factually incorrect.
The word passes no judgment on how the mistake got there — no lie is implied, no carelessness proven.
It simply stamps the entry false.
That even-handedness is why reports, captions, and beliefs get called erroneous, while the people who hold them are merely mistaken.
Erroneous is the formal stamp for entries, figures, reports, and beliefs that are factually incorrect — the auditor's and editor's word.
People are mistaken, never erroneous.
Note the line between it and this unit's simplistic: a simplistic account may be accurate as far as it goes, just thinner than the truth; an erroneous one states what is false.

The family had never owned a cabin, lakeside or otherwise, and had the deeds to prove where they had always lived.

It took one afternoon at the county office to find the source: a clerk in 1998 had keyed a parcel number one digit off, and the erroneous record had been copied forward, database to database, for twenty-five years.
No one had ever checked it against the ground truth.
The county apologized, cancelled the bill, and — the clerk's modern successor admitted — found three more families in the same file.
